quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the road is wet.
The road ahead has curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and keep more distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It raises the chance of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It does not affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It raises the chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can affect how your brain works and make it harder to drive safely. Mixing alcohol with other drugs increases crash risk.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many types of drugs can hurt your ability to drive. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: At night, when should you dim your headlights for an oncoming car?

options.text: When the car is 500 feet away.
When the car is 400 feet away.
When the car is 450 feet away.
When the car is 350 feet away.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the car is 500 feet away.
questions.explanation: Switch to low beam headlights when an oncoming car is 500 feet away.

questions.question: Where can you not park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a bike lane.
Within 12 inches of the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bike lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane. When parking on the street, park within 12 inches of the road's edge.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you go faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. At high speeds, your tires lose grip and the car slides on a layer of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back quickly.
Ease off the gas, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease off the gas, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Take your foot off the gas and steer the car parallel to the road. Slow down and carefully steer back on with both hands on the wheel. Check for traffic before steering back onto the road.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You can go when the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians and it is safe.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a cyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Wait for the car to pass, then pass the cyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the car to pass, then pass the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Deal with one hazard at a time. When there is an oncoming car and a cyclist you want to pass, let the car go first. Then pass the cyclist.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Protecting yourself by passing slow drivers.
Staying close behind the car in front of you.
Quickly changing lanes to get through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you watch for danger and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with bad drivers or dangerous pedestrians.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers be prepared for?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need a longer distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Drivers should stay where the truck driver can see them and where they can see the road ahead clearly.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: This action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means an action is forbidden. These signs are white and rectangular with red and black markings.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use half a lane.
Pass in the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same rights as other vehicles. Always give a motorcycle a complete lane width so it has room to move safely.

questions.question: Which of these must you follow first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come before signs, signals, and road markings. This includes police officers, fire police, work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: When passing a large truck in a small car, be ready for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind from the truck.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create wind gusts strong enough to push smaller cars. Drivers should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Move to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic going in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of the above
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, your weight, and the time between drinks. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment from drinking too much.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is coming, and you should watch for trains.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a defect that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have the money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe driving must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: When you drive past a car that just parked on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
Expect the driver to wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When you pass a parked car, be ready for the driver to open the door. Drive carefully near parked vehicles.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic.
When you are in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly and blocking traffic is illegal. You can get a ticket for driving slower than the normal traffic flow.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The full lane width, just like other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same full lane width as other vehicles to stay safe.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with more effort, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with more effort, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need more strength to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before you change lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Wait to see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black words on a yellow background. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming car or within 500 feet of a car ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: It is illegal for drivers 21 or older to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers in danger. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive faster because they are more alert.
Take time to calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Your mind will focus on other things instead of the road. Calm down and focus before you drive.

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, a driver should:

options.text: Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop in the intersection to see traffic 200 feet away in both directions.
Stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersection where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
